lemon-hill.description: Lemon Hill is East Fairmount Park's historic mansion and hilltop landscape, currently closed to public use during post-Fan-Festival breakdown and restoration planning.
lemon-hill.location: Use the mansion pin at 1 Lemon Hill Drive. The hill sits above Kelly Drive in East Fairmount Park and is separate from Belmont Plateau, Memorial Hall and the West Park attractions.
lemon-hill.parking: Do not drive to Lemon Hill while the park is closed. Event breakdown and restoration work can control Lemon Hill Drive, nearby park roads and curb access; choose another Fairmount Park destination until the operator lifts the closure.
lemon-hill.hours: Lemon Hill park is currently closed to the public for FIFA Fan Festival breakdown. Mansion access is also by scheduled visit rather than general park hours. Check the official page before traveling.
lemon-hill.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom available while the Lemon Hill area and mansion are closed. Plan facilities at a confirmed-open destination elsewhere in Fairmount Park.
lemon-hill.fees: There is no general public visit while the closure is in effect. Future mansion tours or programs may require reservations or admission; use the official schedule when access resumes.
lemon-hill.accessibility: Closure fencing and work areas make the current visit unavailable. When the site reopens, confirm the mansion entrance and step-free route because a historic hilltop building and sloping grounds do not provide uniform access.
lemon-hill.dogs: Do not bring pets into the closed area. When ordinary park access resumes, the City's six-foot leash rule will apply outdoors, while the historic house may keep separate animal restrictions.
lemon-hill.family: Skip Lemon Hill as a family destination until the closure is lifted. The City has announced future playground, restoration, tree, lighting and accessibility improvements, but opening dates and finished amenities are not yet published.
lemon-hill.need: This is a real temporary closure, not simply a mansion-hours issue. Recheck the official Lemon Hill page and City improvement updates before making the hill the purpose of a trip.

belmont-plateau.description: Belmont Plateau is West Fairmount Park's broad skyline overlook and open recreation landscape, with picnic space, sports fields and connections toward the Trolley Trail.
belmont-plateau.location: Navigate to Belmont Plateau on Belmont Mansion Drive, not the broad Fairmount Park pin. The skyline lawn is in West Fairmount Park, north of the Mann Center and west of the Schuylkill River.
belmont-plateau.parking: Use legal spaces serving Belmont Mansion Drive and the plateau, then follow posted event restrictions. Roots Picnic and other large events can close roads, reserve lots and change rideshare or pedestrian approaches.
belmont-plateau.hours: Use the open lawn and trail connections during daylight; City parks have a 10 p.m. curfew and trails are dawn to dusk. Permitted events, field reservations, gates and maintenance can control the plateau independently.
belmont-plateau.restrooms: Do not count on a permanently open restroom at the overlook. Restroom access may be tied to an event, permitted field or seasonal facility, so confirm before settling in for a long picnic.
belmont-plateau.fees: Ordinary overlook, lawn and trail access is free. Ticketed festivals, permitted gatherings, vendors and reserved sports use are separate.
belmont-plateau.accessibility: The primary arrival reaches a broad open plateau, but grass, slopes, curb transitions, event barriers and natural-surface trail connections vary. Confirm the event layout when visiting during a festival.
belmont-plateau.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary open park areas under the City's six-foot leash rule. Keep pets out of active fields, event-controlled areas and any posted animal-free zones.
belmont-plateau.family: The skyline view and open lawn work for a picnic or short family stop, but this is not a fenced playground. Bring shade and water, supervise near roads and fields, and verify restroom availability.
belmont-plateau.need: Belmont Plateau changes character during major festivals and sports events. Check the City event calendar, road restrictions and weather before relying on a normal parking or picnic setup.

fairmount-water-works.description: Fairmount Water Works is the free watershed education center and historic riverfront complex below the Philadelphia Museum of Art, with exhibits and outdoor Schuylkill views.
fairmount-water-works.location: Navigate to 640 Waterworks Drive below the art museum. The entrance is at river level beside the Schuylkill, not at the Rocky Steps or the upper museum plaza.
fairmount-water-works.parking: The operator lists free two-hour parking along Waterworks Drive. Spaces and vehicle access can change for events, flooding and road closures, so use SEPTA, PHLASH or a backup garage when the riverfront is busy.
fairmount-water-works.hours: The interpretive center is open Wednesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Outdoor riverfront paths may be accessible more broadly, but exhibits, restrooms and staff follow building hours.
fairmount-water-works.restrooms: Use visitor facilities during interpretive-center hours. Do not assume the building is open on Sunday through Tuesday or after 5 p.m. simply because the river path is accessible.
fairmount-water-works.fees: General admission is free and donations are welcome. Groups of 10 or more must schedule in advance, with recommended group and tour donations published by the operator.
fairmount-water-works.accessibility: The operator currently reports no elevator access because of Hurricane Ida flood damage. Contact Water Works before a visit requiring elevator service or a specific exhibit route.
fairmount-water-works.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the interpretive center. Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park paths where posted; confirm service-animal access with the operator.
fairmount-water-works.family: The turbine, watershed exhibits, short film and river setting can make a strong free family stop. Confirm the Wednesday-Saturday schedule and elevator limitation before arriving with a stroller or mobility need.
fairmount-water-works.need: Separate the free exhibits from the outdoor riverfront. Building access is limited to Wednesday-Saturday, and the elevator remains unavailable; flooding or city events can also affect Waterworks Drive.

smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.description: Smith Memorial Playground and Playhouse is a free 6.5-acre family destination with more than 50 outdoor play structures, a three-level indoor Playhouse and the Ann Newman Giant Wooden Slide.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.location: Navigate to 3500 Reservoir Drive in East Fairmount Park. Smith is about one-third mile inside the park from the 33rd Street and Oxford Street transit approach.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.parking: A free lot sits in front of the Playhouse. When it fills, the operator allows parking along Reservoir Drive; remove valuables and obey all posted restrictions.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.hours: April-September: Tuesday-Friday 10 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10 a.m.-7 p.m. October-March: Tuesday-Sunday 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Closed Mondays; weather may close all or part, and the Playhouse closes one hour before the Playground in spring and summer.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.restrooms: Restrooms are available as part of the staffed Playground and Playhouse visit. Do not rely on them before opening, after closing or during a weather closure.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.fees: Daily family visits are free. Advance reservations and fees apply to groups of more than 10 children, and rentals or special events are separate.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.accessibility: Smith describes inclusive indoor and outdoor play, but equipment and terrain vary by age and ability. Contact staff before visiting for a specific mobility, sensory or accommodation need.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.dogs: Animals are not permitted at Smith. ADA-defined service animals are welcome.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.family: Smith is designed especially for children age 10 and under. Children must remain with an adult, use age-appropriate equipment and stay within sight of their caregiver.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.need: Hours are weather permitting, the Playhouse can close before the outdoor playground, and food options nearby are limited. Bring food if needed, but grilling and barbecuing are prohibited.

shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.description: Shofuso is a ticketed 1.2-acre Japanese house and garden in West Fairmount Park, with timed entry, delicate historic interiors and separate visitor rules.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.address: Lansdowne Drive and Horticultural Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19131
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.sourceLabel: Japan America Society of Greater Philadelphia
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.location: Use the Shofuso pin inside the Centennial District near Lansdowne and Horticultural Drives. It is not the Horticulture Center entrance or the Please Touch Museum lot.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.parking: The operator lists free parking in the nearby lot. Capacity can tighten during Centennial District events, so reserve the timed visit before driving across the park.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.hours: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m.-5 p.m. Entry is by timed ticket and capacity is limited; Shofuso operates rain or shine.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.restrooms: Plan restroom use around the staffed visit and nearby Centennial District facilities. Confirm current access when reserving, especially for a mobility or family need.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.fees: Published admission is $15 for adults and $10 for seniors, children 5-17, college students and teachers. SNAP/EBT and ACCESS admission is $2 for the cardholder plus up to four family members; listed member, military and museum-worker categories are free.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.accessibility: The operator says the historic house is not wheelchair or scooter accessible and is not easily accessible for walkers, canes or prosthetics. Rubber-tipped or softly covered mobility devices are permitted inside; contact staff before booking.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.dogs: Do not expect pets inside the house or garden. Confirm service-animal access and any accommodation directly before purchasing a timed ticket.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.family: The garden can be memorable for children who can move carefully around water, plants and fragile interiors. Timed capacity, house rules and the major mobility limitation should shape the visit.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.need: Reserve a timed ticket; capacity is limited and ordinary photoshoots are not permitted during open hours. The site is open rain or shine, but the historic house has significant mobility barriers.

please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.description: Please Touch Museum is the ticketed children's museum inside Memorial Hall, with interactive exhibits, a historic carousel, two floors of visitor services and its own parking and schedule.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.address: 4231 Avenue of the Republic, Philadelphia, PA 19131
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.location: Navigate to Memorial Hall at 4231 Avenue of the Republic in West Fairmount Park. The museum is separate from Shofuso, the Horticulture Center and Belmont Plateau even though all are in the Centennial District.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.parking: Use the museum's gated lot beside Memorial Hall and check the current parking charge when reserving. Designated accessible spaces are in the adjacent museum lot.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.hours: Closed Monday and Tuesday. Open Wednesday-Saturday 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; first, fourth and fifth Sundays 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; second and third Sundays 11 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Holiday and special-event hours differ, so verify the selected date.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.restrooms: Restrooms are available on both museum floors, with baby-changing stations in select restrooms. A nursing room is on the lower level behind the Creative Arts Studio.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.fees: Admission is ticketed, and reservations are encouraged for visitors and members age 12 months and older. Use the museum's current reservation page for admission, carousel and parking prices rather than an older listing.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.accessibility: The museum documents accessible parking, restrooms on both floors, a nursing room and sensory and accommodation programs. One complimentary personal-care-attendant admission is available on request for an eligible paid visitor or member.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.dogs: ADA-defined service animals are welcome. Emotional-support, comfort and therapy animals are not permitted inside.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.family: This is a purpose-built children's museum with interactive exhibits and a carousel. Reserve ahead, check the day's opening time and build in breaks for food, restrooms and sensory needs.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.need: Sunday opening time changes by week of the month, and holidays or events can override the weekly schedule. Make a reservation for faster entry and confirm current admission, carousel and parking charges.

valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.description: Valley Green Inn and Trailhead is the park's best-known creekside arrival, combining a historic restaurant, direct Forbidden Drive access, limited parking and one of Wissahickon's three permanent public restrooms.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.address: Valley Green Road at Wissahickon Creek, Philadelphia, PA 19128
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.sourceLabel: Friends of the Wissahickon visitor information
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.location: Navigate to the Valley Green Inn and lower trailhead pin on Valley Green Road beside Wissahickon Creek. This is a creek-level arrival on Forbidden Drive, not the upper Valley Green Road parking area.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.parking: Small public parking areas serve both sides of the Valley Green bridge and an upper lot sits farther up Valley Green Road. Spaces fill quickly; use only legal spaces, lock the vehicle and leave no valuables visible.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.hours: Use the trail during daylight under City trail rules. The restaurant, outdoor restroom and any event-controlled access keep their own schedules; confirm the inn directly if food or indoor service is essential.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.restrooms: Friends of the Wissahickon lists a permanent outdoor flushing restroom at Valley Green Inn. Because operating access can change, use it before heading away from the trailhead rather than assuming another restroom along the route.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.fees: Trailhead, bridge-view and Forbidden Drive access are free. Restaurant meals, private events and other services cost separately.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.accessibility: The arrival reaches broad gravel Forbidden Drive at creek level, but parking availability, gravel, bridge transitions and grades from the upper lot vary. Confirm a suitable space and current restroom access before a mobility-dependent trip.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on park trails under the City's six-foot rule. The restaurant and event areas may set separate animal rules; keep dogs clear of diners and narrow bridge traffic.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.family: This is a practical family starting point for a short creek walk because it combines a recognizable landmark, broad trail and restroom. Parking is tight and the creek is not a play or wading area.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.need: Valley Green is popular and can feel full even when other Wissahickon entrances are quiet. Arrive with a backup trailhead, protect valuables and separate park access from restaurant hours or reservations.

forbidden-drive.description: Forbidden Drive is Wissahickon's 5.35-mile broad gravel spine, following the creek through the gorge and connecting trailheads, historic landmarks and steeper color-blazed side trails.
forbidden-drive.sourceLabel: Friends of the Wissahickon maps and directions
forbidden-drive.location: Forbidden Drive extends through most of the park rather than occupying one point. Choose a segment and trailhead on the FOW map; Valley Green, Bells Mill, Northwestern Avenue and the Ridge Avenue end create very different outing lengths.
forbidden-drive.parking: There is no single Forbidden Drive lot. Park at a legal mapped trailhead and avoid Livezey Lane and Kitchen's Lane, which must remain clear for emergency access. Popular lots require a backup plan.
forbidden-drive.hours: City trail regulations open trails dawn to dusk, seven days a week. Curfew, storm damage, restoration work or an entrance closure may shorten access independently.
forbidden-drive.restrooms: Permanent restrooms are at Valley Green Inn, Kitchen's Lane at Forbidden Drive and the Wissahickon Environmental Center. Seasonal portable toilets appear at selected trailheads, but long sections of the route have no facility.
forbidden-drive.fees: Walking and running are free. Bicycle and equestrian permit rules apply to Upper Wissahickon soft trails; nonresident riders age 16 or older pay the published annual permit fee.
forbidden-drive.accessibility: FOW describes Forbidden Drive as gravel, 5.35 miles long, about 25 feet wide on average, with an average 3% grade and obstacles up to three inches. It is the park's most predictable route, but surface, drainage and trailhead transitions still vary.
forbidden-drive.dogs: Dogs are welcome on a leash no longer than six feet. Keep right, manage the leash around cyclists and horses, and pick up waste.
forbidden-drive.family: A short out-and-back from Valley Green or another mapped trailhead is easier than committing to the full route. Set a turnaround point, carry water and keep children out of the creek.
forbidden-drive.need: The route is shared by walkers, runners, bicycles and horses, with a seven-mile-per-hour trail speed limit and pedestrians holding right of way. Download the map before entering because cellular service is inconsistent.

devil-s-pool.description: Devil's Pool is a natural pool at the Cresheim Creek confluence, reached only by trail and best treated as a scenic waypoint because swimming, wading, jumping and vehicle access on Livezey Lane are prohibited.
devil-s-pool.address: Devil's Pool Trail, Wissahickon Valley Park, Philadelphia, PA 19119
devil-s-pool.sourceLabel: Friends of the Wissahickon visitor information
devil-s-pool.location: The pool lies off the trail near the confluence of Cresheim and Wissahickon Creeks, more than half a mile from the nearest legal trailhead. Follow the official map and remain on the marked approach.
devil-s-pool.parking: There is no legal parking or drop-off on Livezey Lane; it is emergency access. FOW recommends legal alternatives such as the Mt. Airy Avenue trailhead or Henry Avenue between the Summit and Wigard trailheads.
devil-s-pool.hours: Visit only during daylight trail hours and leave enough time for the return hike. Storms, high water, ice, erosion or restoration can close the approach even when the broader park is open.
devil-s-pool.restrooms: There is no restroom at Devil's Pool. Use one of the park's three permanent facilities before hiking, and remember that the nearest legal trailhead is more than half a mile away.
devil-s-pool.fees: Trail access is free. No ticket, reservation or paid activity authorizes swimming or vehicle access on Livezey Lane.
devil-s-pool.accessibility: The trail approach includes natural surfaces, rock, roots, grades and potentially slick edges; it is not a step-free destination. Limited cell service and the distance from emergency access increase the consequence of a fall.
devil-s-pool.dogs: Dogs must remain on a leash no longer than six feet and out of the water. Manage the leash carefully on rock, narrow approaches and crowded viewpoints.
devil-s-pool.family: This is not a splash pad or swimming hole. Families should choose it only for children able to manage the trail and follow water-edge rules; Forbidden Drive is a simpler first Wissahickon outing.
devil-s-pool.need: Swimming and wading are illegal and dangerous because of currents, submerged objects, water quality and wet rock. Do not jump, climb toward the water or block Livezey Lane, and carry all trash out.

thomas-mill-covered-bridge.description: Thomas Mill Covered Bridge is the only surviving covered bridge in the Wissahickon, a red pedestrian landmark beside Forbidden Drive reached as part of a trail outing rather than by driving across it.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.address: Thomas Mill Road Trail at Forbidden Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19118
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.location: The bridge crosses Wissahickon Creek near Forbidden Drive in the northern valley. Use the official park map to choose a trailhead and approach on foot, bicycle or permitted horse; the landmark is not a public motor-vehicle crossing.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.parking: There is no dedicated visitor lot at the bridge. Choose a legal mapped trailhead for the northern park, keep emergency routes clear and calculate the walk from that exact entrance before leaving.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.hours: Reach the bridge during daylight trail hours. High water, ice, fallen trees or trail work can affect the approach independently of the broader park curfew.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.restrooms: There is no public restroom at the bridge. Identify a permanent restroom at the Environmental Center, Kitchen's Lane or Valley Green before beginning the hike.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.fees: Viewing and crossing the bridge as part of a normal trail visit is free. Bicycle and equestrian permit rules may apply on connecting Upper Wissahickon soft trails.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.accessibility: The bridge is a trail landmark with gravel and natural-surface approaches; route and grade depend on the selected trailhead. Do not assume a step-free approach based only on the bridge deck.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the trail and bridge under the City's six-foot rule. Yield at the narrow covered span and keep pets away from horses and the creek edge.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.family: The red bridge makes a rewarding family landmark if the selected hike matches children's distance and terrain ability. Bring water, identify a restroom first and supervise at the creek.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.need: Download the map and choose the complete out-and-back route before starting. The nearby historic fountain is sealed and is not a drinking-water source.

fingerspan.description: Fingerspan is Jody Pinto's 59-foot weathering-steel sculpture and footbridge on the Orange Trail, spanning a steep ravine reached by rocky trail and WPA stone stairs.
fingerspan.address: Orange Trail between Livezey Lane and Mt. Airy Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19119
fingerspan.location: Fingerspan sits on the Orange Trail between Livezey Lane and Mt. Airy Avenue, above a steep ravine. Follow the official trail map and blazes; it is not visible from a parking lot or Forbidden Drive.
fingerspan.parking: Use a legal mapped trailhead such as Mt. Airy Avenue and hike to the bridge. Do not use Livezey Lane for parking or drop-off because it is reserved for emergency access.
fingerspan.hours: Visit in daylight trail hours and leave time for the rocky return. The Orange Trail approach may close for erosion, fallen trees, ice or restoration even when Forbidden Drive remains open.
fingerspan.restrooms: There is no restroom at Fingerspan or on its immediate Orange Trail approach. Use a confirmed permanent facility before starting and carry what you need.
fingerspan.fees: The trail and public artwork are free to visit. No reservation is required for an ordinary hike.
fingerspan.accessibility: The destination is not step-free: its approach uses a narrow natural-surface trail, grades, rock and stone stairs, and the bridge has a grated deck over a deep ravine. Choose Forbidden Drive for a more predictable surface.
fingerspan.dogs: Dogs must stay on a leash no longer than six feet. Keep the leash short on stairs, the grated bridge and narrow trail, and yield to oncoming hikers.
fingerspan.family: Fingerspan can be memorable for experienced young hikers, but it is not a casual stroller outing. Children need close supervision on stone stairs, the grated span and steep terrain.
fingerspan.need: Download the map before entering and do not improvise a shortcut from Livezey Lane. Wet leaves, ice and low light make the stairs and rock approach substantially harder.

dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.description: Dilworth Park Fountain is a 241-jet, zero-depth water feature over the transit concourse, animated by Janet Echelman and OLIN's Pulse artwork with colored mist that follows subway movement below.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.location: The fountain occupies the broad central plaza on City Hall's west side, between the 15th Street transit headhouses and the Greenfield Lawn. Use the exact fountain pin rather than the larger City Hall complex.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.parking: There is no dedicated park parking. Arrive by SEPTA or use a paid Center City garage; curb spaces are limited and loading, construction or events can change nearby access.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.hours: The fountain operates seasonally from April through October, weather permitting. It may pause for maintenance, events or unsafe conditions even while Dilworth Park remains open from 6 a.m. to 1 a.m.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.restrooms: Public bathrooms are inside City Hall and their hours vary. There is no restroom in the fountain plaza, so confirm City Hall access before changing clothes or planning a long family visit.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.fees: Fountain and Pulse viewing is free. Food, drinks, ticketed programs and winter attractions cost separately.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.accessibility: The plaza has barrier-free street-level paths and the fountain is a flush, zero-depth surface. Wet paving can be slippery, and not every transit line below City Hall is yet fully accessible; choose the exact SEPTA entrance for the line you need.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.dogs: Dogs must remain on a leash no longer than six feet and stay out of the fountain. The adjacent Greenfield Lawn also excludes dogs.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.family: This is an urban water-play space rather than a fenced splash pad. Bring a change of clothes, supervise around moving pedestrians and wet paving, and identify an open City Hall restroom before play begins.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.need: Pulse mist and fountain jets are operational features, not guaranteed continuous performances. Check the operator's current park update and weather before making water play the purpose of a trip.

rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.description: Rothman Orthopaedics Ice Rink is Dilworth Park's seasonal outdoor skating rink, installed over the fountain plaza during the winter program and operated with timed sessions and separate admission.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.location: The rink replaces the central fountain footprint on the west side of City Hall. Enter from 15th Street and follow the current winter layout for admission, rentals and the session queue.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.parking: There is no rink lot. SEPTA is the simplest arrival; otherwise use a paid Center City garage and allow extra time for holiday traffic, event closures and limited curb access.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.hours: The rink generally operates from mid-November through late February, but daily sessions, holiday hours and weather closures change by season. Use the current winter schedule before traveling.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.restrooms: Public bathrooms are inside City Hall and hours vary. Winter structures may offer changing or service space but should not be treated as a guaranteed public restroom.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.fees: Skating and rentals are ticketed separately from free park access. Do not rely on a prior season's prices, discounts or reservation rules; check the current winter program when it is published.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.accessibility: Barrier-free plaza paths reach the rink perimeter. Contact the current operator before booking for adaptive skating, transfer needs or a non-skating companion accommodation because session procedures can change.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.dogs: Dogs may pass through permitted park areas on a six-foot leash but cannot enter the ice. Crowds, skate traffic and temporary winter structures make this a poor pet destination.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.family: Choose a session suited to the skaters' ability, reserve if the current season requires it and arrive early enough for check-in and rentals. Gloves and weather layers matter even on mild days.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.need: The rink does not operate year-round and can close for rain, warmth, ice maintenance or a private event. Confirm the same-day session before leaving and separate rink hours from the park's broader 6 a.m.-1 a.m. schedule.

albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.description: Albert M. Greenfield Lawn is Dilworth Park's 6,900-square-foot seasonal lawn and shaded seating area, transformed into the Wintergarden with plantings, lights and gathering space during the colder season.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.sourceLabel: Center City District 2026 Dilworth Park fact sheet
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.location: The lawn sits immediately north of the fountain on City Hall's west apron, near the Dilworth Park Cafe and tree groves. Seasonal installations can change its edges and entrances.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.parking: There is no dedicated lawn parking. Use SEPTA or a paid Center City garage and check for City Hall events that may restrict nearby streets or plaza access.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.hours: The park is open 6 a.m.-1 a.m., but the lawn is seasonal and can close for recovery, maintenance, private events or conversion to the Wintergarden. Programs keep their own published times.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.restrooms: Public bathrooms are inside City Hall and hours vary. Confirm access before settling in for a long visit, especially with children.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.fees: Ordinary lawn and Wintergarden access is free. Food, drinks, ticketed attractions and some special events are separate.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.accessibility: Barrier-free paved paths reach the lawn perimeter and seasonal garden. Grass, movable furniture, crowds and temporary event surfaces can be less predictable than the surrounding plaza.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.dogs: Dogs are not allowed on the Greenfield Lawn. Leashed dogs may use other permitted park paths, but temporary events can impose tighter controls.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.family: The lawn is useful for a short break near the fountain, while the Wintergarden offers a seasonal walk-through setting. It is not a fenced play area, so supervise children around plaza traffic and event equipment.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.need: Do not assume the lawn is available because the park is open. Recovery periods and seasonal conversions can close the grass; check the current program if lawn seating is important.

dilworth-park-transit-entrances.description: Dilworth Park's glass transit headhouses and elevators connect the plaza to SEPTA's 15th Street Market-Frankford/Trolley station complex and the wider City Hall concourse, with accessibility differing by line and entrance.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.address: 15th Street and Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.sourceLabel: SEPTA City Hall and 15th Street Station Accessibility Program
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.location: Use the glass headhouses and marked elevators along the park's 15th Street edge. Follow signs for the exact Market-Frankford, trolley or Broad Street service rather than assuming every entrance reaches every platform directly.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.parking: Transit is the intended arrival. If driving, use a paid Center City garage; the park has no public lot and curb access can be restricted by buses, loading, construction or events.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.hours: Station entrances follow SEPTA service and temporary closure schedules, not the park's 6 a.m.-1 a.m. hours. Verify the line and elevator status for the time of travel.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.restrooms: Do not expect a public restroom in the SEPTA concourse. Public bathrooms are inside City Hall with varying hours.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.fees: Entering the park is free; SEPTA fare is required beyond station fare lines. Use SEPTA's current fare information rather than an older listing.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.accessibility: The completed 15th Street work provides elevators for Market-Frankford and trolley access, while full Broad Street Line accessibility at City Hall remains an active SEPTA project. Check elevator status and the exact accessible route before traveling.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.dogs: Pets on SEPTA must follow the agency's current carrier and service-animal rules. A dog permitted on park paths is not automatically permitted aboard transit without meeting those rules.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.family: The direct transit arrival avoids parking, but the concourse is large and line transfers can be confusing. Decide the correct exit before boarding and keep children close around platforms, escalators and the busy plaza.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.need: City Hall and 15th Street are connected but not uniformly accessible across every line. Use SEPTA's current concourse map and elevator alerts, and allow extra transfer time rather than choosing an entrance only because it is closest.
